evidence: Every plural/'only'/'exactly one'/'unchanged' instance was enumerated and checked against the whole collection and against legitimate side effects of the same operation. (1) Plural asks graded across the whole set. Constraints gate: 'exactly one card for that candidate in Applied' is checked across the whole Applied stage. hro_add_candidate: all six J1 cards A-F 'in the order added'. hro_bulk_move: all three of Y, W, X in board order, plus the A2, V mixed-stage pair; 'only some move' fails it. hro_bulk_all_or_none and hro_bulk_places: 'none of the set moves' / 'any of the three enters', by both the UI and replay; this matches rules lines 91-92 ('Every card must satisfy all the rules... If any card fails, none of them moves'). hro_undo_restores: Y, W, X all back at their places (Y, W, X, Z, A2), matching rules line 96 ('every card of that move back'). hro_undo_conflict: refused 'each time' for both a move and a reorder, and fails if it 'partly applies'. hro_activity: 'every successful board action performed on J1 and J2 before A, by any account used in this review ... each card of every single and multi-card move ... every undo', and the filter 'shows all of that job's lines and only those'; this matches rules lines 110-112 ('Every job opening, added candidate, move...'). hro_activity_refusals: 'none of the refused attempts in this review added a line'. hro_candidate_private: 'no response a candidate page receives', backed by protocol K 'Capture every request the candidate page makes and inspect every response'; this matches rules line 192 ('Nothing a candidate's browser receives'). hro_candidate_view: 'each candidate's own applications all appear'. hro_thread_earlier: '30 at a time ... until none remain'. hro_mgr_late_stages, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_observer_readonly and hro_anonymous use 'each'/'any of these' over enumerated lists. hro_restart covers jobs, card order per stage, notes, messages and activity. hro_drafts checks two conversations with distinct drafts, matching rules line 174 ('Each conversation keeps its own draft'). hro_thread_access's 'every recruiter ... every conversation' (rules line 131) is sampled with two recruiters on one conversation. Mei is not J2's opener, so a job-owner-only bug is still caught. The criterion names its sample explicitly ('recruiters (Rafael, Mei)') and does not claim 'every'. (2) The 'unchanged / nothing changes' guards are scoped so they do not punish legitimate side effects. functional/prompt.md line 19 limits the guard to 'card, order, message or note' and an Activity line, and deducts a refused action's line only in hro_activity_refusals. Rules line 53 ('A refused move changes nothing') and line 113 ('A refused action adds no entry') make that guard public. hro_undo_restores explicitly exempts a note as a non-change ('goes ahead after a note was added'), matching rules line 99. hro_unread_counts uses state-relative wording ('rises by exactly two', 'computed from the observed sequence') instead of absolute counts. For Mei's count it states which messages count, which tolerates Mei's own message, Bill's and others. hro_pol_live_board guards against 'reset' scroll, not any scroll change. hro_pol_live_thread requires the view to stay at the newest message and show Noor's message, so legitimate auto-scroll at the bottom is expected, not penalised. Concurrency cannot create spurious changes: test.sh run_suite uses 'rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1', so polish and visual activity does not land inside functional's U or D readings. The golden writes one Activity line per card (index.js:315 inside the per-card loop; index.js:366 for each undone card), so the reference satisfies hro_activity's per-card wording. Weak-app probes: an app that moves only the first selected card, or applies a partial bulk set, fails hro_bulk_move and hro_bulk_all_or_none. An app that logs only the first card of a bulk move fails hro_activity. An app that undoes only one card fails hro_undo_restores. An app that leaks notes only in a secondary candidate response fails hro_candidate_private, because every response is inspected. Conforming-alternative probes: an app that refuses before sending passes through the replay paths. An app that hides refused controls passes ('hiding it is optional'). An app that blocks undo of a reorder after a later move stays consistent with rules line 99-100. Residual P3 observations, not defects: (a) hro_activity's 'each card of every single and multi-card move' could lead a strict judge to demand one line per card, or per-card from-stages, from an app that writes one combined line such as 'Rafael moved A2 and V to Screen'. The spec (rules lines 110-111) asks only for 'a readable line' per move, with who and what changed. A combined line that names every card and its stages satisfies the wording, and only one that omits the from-stages of a mixed-stage set is at risk. (b) hro_restart says 'activity lines are unchanged'. An unusual app that logs sign-ins in Activity would add a line on the fresh sign-in. The criterion's failure clause ('lost, reordered or duplicated') shows that preservation is the intent. (c) hro_pol_session_resume checks Mei against one conversation draft and one note draft. Rules line 174 says 'sees none of them', but a per-user draft scope is all-or-nothing in practice. None of these is a credible misgrade that needs a fix before delivery.
